about: Exo identity spec v0 (plan §2; §2.14 lists what changed in /2, §2.15 in /3, §2.16 in /4, §2.18 in /5, §2.19 in /6, §2.7's sync wire and §2.17's profile items in /7, §2.7's rules 6 to 8 in /8: the new sync key after a removal, the link messages and the device list carried in profile items, §2.18's one take under the mutex in /9: two apps on one PC taking one fork sign it again once, §2.17's account.sealed in /10, its profile banner in /11, the account entry and restricted PCs in /12, restricted PCs reaching only restricted PCs and account-box.sealed in /13, the account entry's add after the owner left and the profile's look in /14, the profile's canvas, a media's view, accent2, font and the longer lists in /15, a setup block's gear and build, the hero as blocks, a font on any block and the 96 grid in /16, the profile's stats, watching and the watching showcase in /17, the look and canvas as one item per field, who sees a block, hidden games and what a PC carries across a sign-out in /18, the profile's media (its parts' names and seals, a media request's signed bytes, its box rows) and no JSON nulls (a field with none is left out) in /19). Bytes are lowercase hex unless a field says otherwise; JSON records are as they travel. Every signature is low-s. HPKE itself is checked against RFC 9180 A.3.1.

cases.rule: 1. a remove beats any concurrent change by the device it removes
cases.head: 34915df6b23534611e7640abca842211c6ac28c16dcb7a9a4e9202cd29f155f2

cases.rule: 2. two devices remove each other: the one added earlier wins, so a stolen PC added first beats a newer one (the recovery code takes it back: case 6)
cases.head: 34915df6b23534611e7640abca842211c6ac28c16dcb7a9a4e9202cd29f155f2

cases.rule: 3. otherwise the lower hash wins; the loser's author signs it again on top with the next seq and the new head as prev, keeping its at
cases.head: 8630b700599638c289f5a58ae45fa7709f93ef53d7d02a0d34007b56ba105485

cases.rule: 4. a three-way cycle (pairwise: A's remove beats B's rename, B's beats C's by hash, C's beats A's by hash): B is struck, then the lower hash of what's left; the losers are signed again in rank order, so A's remove of B goes first and B's rename is dropped
cases.head: 084829cb64986d6716905b337defa23d78bb9e0bd6f4c5fd5ccba6fecb1f0bda

cases.rule: 5. four at once (B and A remove each other, C renames, D removes C): A strikes B, D strikes C, then the lower hash of A's and D's; in rank order A's remove of B is signed again first, so B's remove of A (lower hash) is dropped
cases.head: 18c4715fae899d7d30cd520719639892c4e31ccd33179c93b44bf7491a299b19

cases.rule: 6. the recovery code in the race of case 2: it ranks before every PC, so its remove strikes A (the stolen PC added first) and the lower hash of R's and B's wins
cases.head: 0ea4018f5a5e9eccd77588745635cbc55f3dc1268c83284a4ff6ed36b22fe9f1

droppedOnResign.why: the device it removes is gone

cases.rule: 7. a losing branch of three is signed again in order by its author, each change keeping its content and at; one that no longer applies (it renames C, which the winner removed) is dropped and the rest go on
cases.head: 72c990b6838b78306611db2c24b92bd82fa538b0134d8ea1a34ae3acf74c8eed

droppedOnResign.why: the device it renames is gone

cases.rule: 8. two losers that still apply, by different authors: each is signed again on top of the new head in its author's rank order, one after another (B's, then C's on top of it), whatever their hashes or arrival order
cases.head: 03a7bd3d40e19123c2960230c144afe4763a2f35e9a98a96cf8548bdff7d9216

cases.rule: 9. equivocation: C signs two different changes after the same head; whoever sees both drops both (in either order) and marks C, which stays listed; D's change wins, and C's next change at a higher seq counts again
cases.head: e15e4e25dc5aec0c7d2c61b654288c8a3d7d290b5dcbd438668cbc0a2a170847

takeChanges.take: one hold of stateMutex: take device-list.json's changes into the list the app read, then the profile's changes in seq order (one that comes before the change it follows is tried again once that one is in), sign this PC's own changes that lost a fork again (passing over an action already on the chain), write device-list.json, let go
takeChanges.compare: A port's own re-sign has another signature: compare the first step's resigned and after without each change's sig, and verify the sig. The later steps take the file's bytes further: compare them whole.

accountEntry.about: The account entry has "account": true and only adds PCs. A PC it adds is restricted, and so is any PC a restricted PC adds: it removes and renames only itself and restricted PCs whose add comes after its own (never a PC the owner brought in, however late), and adds no entry. A PC that isn't restricted adds the account entry when there is none and removes it (account sign-in off); the recovery entry removes it too. AccountNumber counts account entries ever added; its kits carry it, as CodeNumber does the recovery code's.

rejoin.about: The account entry's add is restricted while a PC that isn't restricted is listed, or the recovery entry is. With neither (the owner signed out of their last PC, or reinstalled), it isn't. Neither entry counts as a PC; a restricted PC's add stays restricted. Restricted is read from the chain as merged: an add that loses a fork and is signed again on top can change.
